text.p: Highlands Gold Ltd said on Thursday its directors had formally rejected the takeover bid by Placer Dome Inc after an independent report showed Highlands' shares to be worth about 40 percent more than the 75 cent per share offer price made by Placer Dome.
Highlands described the offer as totally inadequate, saying a report by investment bank Barings Brothers Burrows had valued Highlands shares at 96 cents to A$1.14.

Highlands chairman Clive Hildebrand said company representatives had held "initial inconclusive discussions" with Placer on an alternative proposal for it to purchase Highlands' 25 percent stake in the Porgera gold mine in Papua New Guinea.

"Highlands will only agree to an outcome so long as the terms and structures of the resulting transaction are attractive to Highlands shareholders," Hildebrand said. "Any transaction of this nature would be subject to shareholder approval."
Placer, which launched its initial bid in November, said late last month it was willing to cancel its interests in Highlands and instead pay A$276.8 million for the Porgera stake.
Highlands repeated that the 75 cents takeover offer did not recognise the value of its Frieda-Nena copper/gold project and Ramu nickle/cobalt project, or its exploration portfolio.

"With 43,000 Highlands shareholders and significant shareholdings held by PNG financial institutions, Placer is unlikely to gain sufficient acceptances from its totally inadequate takeover terms to acquire 100 percent of Highlands," it said.
Placer said on December 30 it had raised its stake in Highlands to 40.8 percent from an initial stake of 33.3 percent.
Placer currently holds a 25 percent stake in Porgera through its listed Placer Pacific Ltd unit, for which Placer Dome is also making a takeover offer.
The other equal partners in Porgera are Goldfields Ltd and PNG interests, held 15 percent by Orogen Minerals Ltd and 10 percent by the government's Minerals Development Resources Corp (MRDC).
